# Pi magic 8-ball: contract and design

## Contents

- [Design](#design)
- [Contract](#contract)
- [Evidence and usability improvements](#improvements)
- [Optional transcripts](#transcripts)
- [Builder reasoning and evidence discovery](#discovery)
- [Verification and remaining limits](#verification)


## Design {#design}

V1 adds one advisory choice tool. It uses a separate chat-model loop to collect neutral state, then Pi's classifier API.
Jev and Clef use the same backend boundary. Model selection stays in extension-owned settings files and user-issued slash commands, not model-issued arguments.
The builder has no inherited extensions, filesystem writes, shell, web, or classifier access. Its transcript stays in memory.
The parent session stores returned state and results through normal Pi tool-result persistence. Configured providers receive permitted context and state.
Read scopes restrict collection, not provider retention. Users must select providers suitable for their data.
Prompt instructions request neutrality. Schema validation cannot prove neutrality, factual accuracy, completeness, or secret removal.

Implementation safety ceilings are 4 builder requests, 8 evidence calls, 2048 output tokens per builder request, and 120000 milliseconds per invocation.
These ceilings bound work, not monetary cost or confidence calibration. The extension makes no application-level retries or model fallbacks.
Conversation input holds at most 24000 UTF-8 bytes. A workspace result holds at most 16000 UTF-8 bytes.
State holds at most 12000 UTF-8 bytes. Truncation is explicit. Oversized or malformed final state fails closed.
Git execution, research, boolean questions, and score questions are outside V1.

## Contract {#contract}

`magic8ball({ question, responses, abstain?, context? })` returns a structured success or error.
`context` has boolean `conversation` and `workspace` fields. Both default to true.
Optional `context.files` supplies workspace-relative file hints. REQ-12 defines their validation.
Unknown fields and non-booleans are invalid.
`abstain` defaults to true. Explicit false disables the added `insufficient_evidence` response.
Both configured models require provider and model identifiers. The extension never uses the parent model as a fallback.
User settings live in `<Pi agent directory>/magic8ball.json`, normally `~/.pi/agent/magic8ball.json`.
Trusted project settings live in `<cwd>/.pi/magic8ball.json`. Each role is a complete `{ "provider": "...", "model": "..." }` pair.
A project role overrides the entire user role. Partial pairs do not inherit individual fields. Untrusted project files are not read.
The four former `PI_MAGIC8BALL_*` model-selection variables are ignored. Provider credentials remain in Pi's authentication system.
`/magic8ball` opens an interactive two-model picker. `/magic8ball show` displays settings and their sources.
`/magic8ball builder <provider> <model>` and `/magic8ball classifier <provider> <model>` update one role.
A single `--project` or `--global` flag may precede or follow command arguments; saves default to user scope.
In noninteractive mode, `/magic8ball` displays usage and settings without writing. Picker cancellation never writes.

<a id="REQ-1"></a>

**REQ-1**

The tool MUST validate inputs before model calls. The question and every response description MUST be nonempty strings after trimming.
Response identifiers MUST match `[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,63}` and exclude `__proto__`, `prototype`, `constructor`, and `insufficient_evidence`.
The caller MUST supply 2–25 responses with abstention, or 2–26 without it. The tool MUST preserve identifiers and descriptions.
The serialized request MUST contain at most 16000 UTF-8 bytes. Invalid domain inputs MUST return `invalid-input` without model calls.
Pi's schema-validation error takes precedence when arguments fail the registered parameter schema before the extension executes.


<a id="AC-1"></a>

**AC-1**

Changed behavior. Valid inputs retain caller criteria and add abstention by default. Explicit false permits 26 caller choices.
Empty descriptions, reserved identifiers, invalid counts, unknown fields, and oversized requests produce `invalid-input` before model calls.


<a id="REQ-2"></a>

**REQ-2**

The builder MUST run before classification with only the permitted conversation and workspace scopes.
It MUST receive neutral-state instructions. Only the three evidence tools MAY be declared when workspace scope is true.
REQ-11 requires an empty tool declaration during finalization.
It MUST NOT receive classifier output from this invocation or prior `magic8ball` tool results.
Final state MUST contain exactly `goal`, `constraints`, `current_state`, `evidence`, and `uncertainties`.
Evidence entries MUST contain exactly nonempty `fact` and `source` strings. Other collections MUST contain only nonempty strings.
The tool MUST reject candidate-keyed state, malformed JSON, extra fields, or state exceeding 12000 bytes as `invalid-state`.


<a id="AC-2"></a>

**AC-2**

Changed behavior. Mock builder and classifier calls show state precedes classification and no classifier feedback reaches the builder.
Workspace-disabled requests expose no evidence tools. Conversation-disabled requests expose no prior messages.
Valid state reaches classification unchanged. Extra recommendation fields, candidate-keyed state, malformed JSON, and oversized state fail before classification.


<a id="REQ-3"></a>

**REQ-3**

The three evidence tools MUST restrict paths to the real workspace root and reject symlinks and special files.
They MUST reject dot-prefixed path segments, `node_modules`, and conventional credential files, including PEM, key, and P12 files.
Listing MUST omit denied paths. Read and literal search MUST operate on one regular UTF-8 text file per call.
REQ-19 permits an absent-path observation without opening a file. This exception does not permit content inspection of restricted or nonregular paths.
Read offset defaults to 1. Read limit defaults to 200 and MUST be in the inclusive range 1–200.
List results MUST contain at most 200 names. Search results MUST contain at most 200 matching lines.
File content inspection MUST read at most 16000 bytes per call. Truncation MUST be explicit.
The builder MUST call evidence tools through `ctx.executeTool` so Pi's validation and permission hooks remain active.
These tools MUST NOT write files, execute workspace code, or invoke other tools.


<a id="AC-3"></a>

**AC-3**

Changed behavior. Temporary-workspace tests confirm bounded read, list, and literal search.
Traversal, external paths, symlinks, hidden credential paths, key files, binary files, and special files fail without exposing content.
Builder tests show only allowlisted evidence names reach the nested-tool boundary. Permission failures stop classification.


<a id="REQ-4"></a>

**REQ-4**

The classifier adapter MUST use the configured catalog entry and Pi's `choice` interface for both Jev and Clef.
A success MUST return `answer`, `probabilities`, backend `confidence`, `abstained`, `advisory: true`, state, models, collection metadata, and usage.
The distribution MUST contain exactly the supplied identifiers, including added abstention. Every probability and confidence MUST be finite and in [0,1].
The probability sum MUST differ from 1 by no more than 0.000001. The selected identifier MUST have maximal probability.
The adapter MUST preserve the backend's choice among tied maxima. It MUST NOT renormalize probabilities or substitute confidence.
A malformed answer MUST return `invalid-answer`. Classifier failures MUST return `classifier-failed` without a decision.


<a id="AC-4"></a>

**AC-4**

Changed behavior. Mock Jev and Clef entries receive identical typed questions and state.
Successful results preserve all probabilities and confidence, including confidence different from winning probability and tied choices.
Missing, extra, negative, nonfinite, unnormalized, or nonmaximal answers fail. Abstention is reported without becoming an execution command.


<a id="REQ-5"></a>

**REQ-5**

The orchestrator MUST stop on cancellation, timeout, builder failure, permission failure, or exhausted request or tool ceilings.
It MUST propagate one combined abort signal to builder requests, evidence tools, and classification.
It MUST return an error without a fabricated answer and retain usage reported by completed model calls, including failed calls.
A valid effective settings object that lacks either model role MUST produce `not-configured` before builder requests. An unavailable catalog entry MUST produce `model-unavailable`.
Invalid settings and access failures are governed by REQ-7.
The builder MUST be a physical chat-model entry. A Pi virtual-model entry MUST produce `model-unavailable` before model requests.
No application-level retry, automatic repair, hidden model fallback, background process, or separate transcript file is permitted.
REQ-19 permits a verified, in-bounds `path-not-found` observation. This is not a failed tool call. The model MAY use that observation to select subsequent evidence calls within the existing ceilings; the orchestrator MUST NOT retry automatically.
Provider-level retry suppression uses `maxRetries: 0` where supported. Provider adapters can have their own transport behavior.


<a id="AC-5"></a>

**AC-5**

Changed behavior. Fault-injection tests exercise missing configuration, unavailable models, builder and classifier failures, cancellation, timeout, and budget exhaustion.
A configured virtual builder model produces `model-unavailable` before any builder or classifier call.
No classifier call follows a builder failure. No request or tool call exceeds its ceiling. Completed-call usage survives errors.


<a id="REQ-6"></a>

**REQ-6**

The package MUST register `magic8ball` as a model-only tool with a structured output schema.
Evidence tools MUST be callable nested tools, inactive by default, with read-only annotations.
The main tool description and each success MUST identify decisions as advisory and confidence as distribution concentration, not correctness probability.
The extension MUST work without terminal UI and MUST return aggregate nested-model usage in Pi's tool result.

<a id="REQ-7"></a>

**REQ-7**

Model selection MUST come only from `magic8ball.json` in Pi's agent directory and, when `ctx.isProjectTrusted()` is true, the current workspace's `.pi` directory.
Settings MUST contain only optional `builder` and `classifier` roles. Each present role MUST contain nonempty `provider` and `model` strings with no whitespace; each identifier MUST contain at most 512 UTF-8 bytes.
Only the builder role MAY also contain optional `reasoning`, as specified in REQ-18. No other fields are permitted.
Project settings MUST replace complete roles, not merge individual fields. A missing file MUST act as an empty settings layer.
Each invocation MUST read a fresh settings snapshot before resolving either model. Missing effective roles MUST return `not-configured` before model requests.
Malformed JSON, invalid fields, or files exceeding 16000 UTF-8 bytes MUST return `invalid-config`; inaccessible files, symlink targets or immediate parent directories, and nonregular files MUST return `settings-unavailable`.
Settings failure MUST NOT fall back to environment variables, the parent model, or another settings layer. Untrusted project files MUST be ignored without opening them.

<a id="REQ-8"></a>

**REQ-8**

The extension MUST register a user-issued `/magic8ball` command with interactive configuration, display, and explicit builder/classifier subcommands.
Saves MUST default to user scope; `--project` MUST require current project trust. Conflicting or repeated scope flags and malformed command arguments MUST fail without writes.
The picker MUST expose physical available chat models for the builder and available classifier entries for the classifier. Explicit identifiers MUST resolve to the same model types before persistence.
Cancelling either picker MUST leave both files unchanged. Noninteractive invocation without identifiers MUST NOT prompt or write.
Successful saves MUST preserve the other role in the selected layer and use a same-directory temporary file followed by atomic replacement.
Writes MUST serialize through Pi's file-mutation queue and an exclusive lock file. Contention with another process, corrupt existing settings, or detected external modification MUST fail rather than overwrite data.
A command MUST report its saved path and effective selections, including project overrides of user settings. The next tool invocation MUST use saved settings without `/reload`.
The command MUST NOT change Pi's active conversation model, store credentials, or issue generation or classification requests. Catalog availability uses Pi's normal authentication boundary.
Filesystem races with nonparticipating writers and power-loss durability are outside the guarantee. A save error with uncertain outcome MUST direct the user to inspect settings before retrying.

<a id="REQ-20"></a>

**REQ-20**

The user command MUST provide argument autocomplete through Pi's registered command API.
It MUST suggest `show`, `builder`, `classifier`, `reasoning`, `transcripts`, `--global`, and `--project` at the command root.
Static choices MUST match the current token by case-sensitive prefix. Completed arguments and separators MUST remain in each replacement value.
Each replacement MUST end with a space so the user can complete the next argument without typing a separator.
Autocomplete MUST accept one scope flag before, between, or after settings arguments. It MUST NOT suggest repeated or conflicting flags.
Scoped commands MUST NOT suggest `transcripts`. Transcript arguments MUST suggest only `on`, `off`, and `show`, without scope flags.
Builder provider/model suggestions MUST use available physical chat entries. Classifier suggestions MUST use available classifier entries.
Providers MUST be distinct and sorted by identifier. Provider matching MUST use a case-insensitive prefix.
Models MUST belong to the completed provider. Model matching MUST use Pi's fuzzyFilter across identifiers and display names.
Reasoning suggestions MUST use the supported levels of the builder targeted by the current scope.
Omitted scope and `--global` MUST use the global builder. Trusted `--project` MUST use the effective builder, including a global builder when no project builder exists.
Autocomplete MUST read a fresh settings snapshot for reasoning. It MUST NOT open untrusted project settings.
Unknown syntax, excess arguments, missing context, missing builders, and failed dynamic lookups MUST return no dynamic suggestions.
Static suggestions MUST remain available without settings or catalogs. Lookup failures MUST NOT display raw errors or trigger a fallback, retry, or notification.
The current session context MUST supply dynamic lookups. Session replacement and shutdown MUST discard it and reject pending results from the prior context.
Autocomplete MUST NOT save settings, change transcript capture or the active model, refresh remote catalogs, execute tools, or make generation/classification requests.
Existing command validation, trust checks, picker behavior, and transcript clearing MUST remain unchanged.


<a id="AC-20"></a>

**AC-20**

Changed behavior. Invoke the registered autocomplete callback for empty and partial arguments, both scope flags, interleaved flags, and transcript actions.
PASS if choices follow REQ-20, replacement values retain prior arguments and separators, and completed or invalid commands suggest no extra positional arguments.
Use mock chat/classifier catalogs with duplicate providers, virtual chat entries, display names, and slash-containing model identifiers.
PASS if provider suggestions are distinct, role-specific, and prefix-filtered. PASS if fuzzy model suggestions preserve complete identifiers within the selected provider.
Use private global/project settings with different builder capabilities. Change files between completions and change project trust.
PASS if reasoning choices follow the write target, manual edits apply on the next completion, and unsupported levels do not appear.
Apply completions with Pi's actual autocomplete provider, including a cursor before existing text. PASS if the command and untouched suffix remain intact.
Inject unavailable settings/catalogs and pending classifier lookups during session replacement and shutdown.
PASS if failures return no dynamic suggestions or raw errors, stale results do not return, and static completion still works.
PASS if completion leaves settings bytes, active model, transcript capture, notifications, and model/tool request counts unchanged.
Preserved behavior. All 53 prior offline checks and strict typechecking MUST pass before and after implementation.
Tests MUST use private settings and mock catalogs. No paid request or live settings change is required.




Known Pi 1.0.4 host limitation: after Tab completes `/magic8ball `, the next Tab can fail to open argument completion.
The host editor routes that key to file completion. Its guard removes the trailing space and rejects the request before the argument callback runs.
Forced file completion also skips command arguments. Changing that guard alone would not fix the routing.

After name completion, type the first letter of a subcommand, wait for the menu, then press Tab.
Use `r`, `b`, `c`, or `t` for reasoning, builder, classifier, or transcripts.
For the full argument menu, press Backspace to remove the trailing space, wait for the command menu, then type Space.
A separate isolated check verified these sequences with Pi's actual Editor and mock terminal dimensions.
Provider-only AC-20 tests do not exercise the editor's keyboard routing.
No installed Pi file changed, and the extension does not replace the editor. The user accepted the manual workaround.

## Evidence and usability improvements {#improvements}

The user requested all six improvements from the code review. This change preserves settings, picker behavior, and advisory-only results.
File hints guide collection. They do not authorize reads or replace permission checks.
Byte ranges use the existing per-call byte ceiling. Eight calls bound total inspected file bytes to 128000 per invocation.
The host packaging contract requires wildcard host peers. Exact development versions and CI define the tested compatibility set instead.

<a id="REQ-11"></a>

**REQ-11**

The builder MUST reserve its last permitted request for final state and declare no evidence tools on that request.
The builder MUST also declare no tools when eight evidence calls have completed.
Each request MUST state its remaining request and evidence-call counts, and whether it must finalize.
The builder MUST reject tool calls during finalization without executing them.
No additional request, repair, or fallback is permitted.


<a id="AC-11"></a>

**AC-11**

Changed behavior. A mock gathers evidence on the first three requests and returns state on request four.
PASS if request four declares no tools, contains the remaining counts, and returns collected state.
After eight evidence calls, PASS if the next request finalizes with no tools.
A finalization tool call MUST fail without executing it.
Preserved behavior. Request and call ceilings, cancellation, usage, and no fallback remain enforced.


<a id="REQ-12"></a>

**REQ-12**

The input MAY contain `context.files`, an array of at most eight distinct permitted workspace-relative file paths.
Omission MUST mean no hints. Empty arrays are permitted. Null, non-arrays, denied paths, duplicates, and workspace-disabled hints MUST fail before models.
The builder MUST receive hints as data and MUST NOT read a hint automatically.
Read and search MAY accept `byteOffset` and `byteLength`.
Offset MUST default to zero and be a nonnegative safe integer. Length MUST default to 16000 and be an integer from 1 through 16000.
Null and invalid ranges MUST fail. The helper MUST inspect only that byte window and report its half-open range and observed file size.
Line numbers and read line offsets MUST refer to the byte window, not the whole file.
A window that starts inside a UTF-8 sequence MUST fail. An incomplete terminal sequence MUST be omitted when more file bytes remain.
Existing path, type, byte, line, and permission restrictions MUST remain active.


<a id="AC-12"></a>

**AC-12**

Changed behavior. Supply valid and invalid file hints and inspect the first builder message.
PASS if valid hints survive unchanged, invalid hints fail before models, and no hint triggers an automatic read.
Read and search a fixture beyond byte 16000. PASS if the requested text and exact inspected range return within the byte ceiling.
Test defaults, EOF, invalid/null ranges, split UTF-8 boundaries, and denied paths with a range.
Preserved behavior. Existing prefix reads, list limits, secret-path rejection, and cancellation checks remain passing.


<a id="REQ-13"></a>

**REQ-13**

The collector MUST assign `conversation` to nonempty permitted conversation and `e1` through `e8` to successful workspace calls.
Collection metadata MUST contain a ledger of IDs, source names, scope, truncation, and inspected byte ranges when available.
The builder MUST receive ledger IDs with each source. State evidence sources MUST equal a ledger ID from this invocation.
Unknown IDs and citations to disabled or empty conversation MUST produce `invalid-state` before classification.
The ledger MUST NOT contain raw file contents. Per-source metadata MUST survive successful results.
This check proves source identity, not claim accuracy or neutrality.

PASS if citations use collector IDs and ranges and truncation survive the result.
Invented IDs, arbitrary paths, and disabled-conversation citations MUST fail before classification.
Preserved behavior. State shape, byte ceiling, and separate builder/classifier stages remain enforced.

## Optional transcripts {#transcripts}

The user requested optional visible transcripts instead of metadata-only debugging.
Capture stays local to the extension runtime. The extension creates no transcript files and adds no transcript to model context.
Ordinary conversation, file content, and model text can contain sensitive data. The capture filter is not a secret detector.

<a id="REQ-17"></a>

**REQ-17**

The user-only `/magic8ball transcripts` command MUST toggle capture. `on` and `off` MUST set capture explicitly.
`/magic8ball transcripts show` MUST display the last captured invocation. Unknown arguments and scope flags MUST fail without settings writes or model requests.
Capture MUST default to off. Session start and shutdown MUST turn it off and clear retained text.
Off MUST clear retained text and revoke in-flight recorders. Repeated on MUST preserve the existing captured invocation.
A new captured invocation MUST replace the prior invocation when it starts. Older concurrent or late completions MUST NOT overwrite it.
Capture MUST include logical Pi builder requests (system prompt, messages, tool declarations), visible builder responses, model-facing evidence results, and classifier requests/responses.
The filter MUST omit thinking/reasoning blocks, signatures, images, authentication fields, request headers, and raw provider error messages.
Failed or aborted builder response text MUST be omitted, because adapters can place raw errors in text blocks.
Only allowlisted evidence argument fields and classifier decision fields MAY enter structured capture. Arbitrary provider-result fields MUST NOT enter it.
The recorder MUST keep at most 128000 UTF-8 bytes of transcript body per invocation, reusing the eight-call by 16000-byte collection ceiling.
Display headers and the bounded failed-call diagnostic footer in REQ-19 are outside the body ceiling.
Overflow MUST clip at a character boundary and report transcript truncation. Capture failures MUST NOT change model work or decision results.
Completion MUST close the recorder. No provider result that arrives after completion MAY append text.
The extension MUST NOT write transcript files, add transcript fields to tool results, append session entries, or send captured text to either model.
The TUI viewer MUST be read-only, scrollable, width/height bounded, and close with Escape or Ctrl+C. RPC show MUST use a user-directed notification.
A disabled or empty capture MUST show fixed status text, not old transcript content. Hosts and clients may retain displayed data outside the extension.
The registered tool schema MUST NOT allow models to enable capture. Settings and picker behavior MUST remain unchanged.


<a id="AC-17"></a>

**AC-17**

Changed behavior. Invoke the user command without valid settings and inspect default, bare toggle, explicit on/off, show, and invalid syntax.
PASS if no command writes settings, performs a model request, or changes Pi's active model.
Run mocked builder/evidence/classifier work with capture on. PASS if show includes actual logical inputs, visible outputs, and source IDs in order.
Inject hidden blocks, signatures, authentication fields, and raw provider errors. PASS if these fields are absent while visible model text remains.
PASS if tool content/details/structuredContent contain no captured transcript or capture-only markers, and disabled capture stores no transcript.
